articleTitle: A Group-Type Distributed Secure Coded Computation Scheme Based on a Secret Sharing
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We focus on a distributed secure coded computation scheme for matrix multiplication. We propose new distributed coded computation schemes and evaluate the computation time complexity, the erasure-correcting capability of the overall system, and the information security.The full version of this paper is in [1].

articleTitle: Bayes Optimal Estimation and Its Approximation Algorithm for Difference with and without Treatment under URLC Model
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the data generative model in which a target population is divided into several latent classes, and the probability distribution of responses within each latent class is the same under a given treatment. We call this model the Uniform Response Latent Class model (URLC model). Under the proposed model, we calculate Bayesian optimal decision and its approximation algorithm for the difference with and without the treatment for the entire population. We conduct experiments and confirm the following characteristics of the proposed algorithm: 1) our algorithm correctly estimates the true number of latent classes even if the number of latent classes is not known. 2) given the synthetic data generated from the proposed model, the mean square error is smaller than the conventional method. 3) when the class tendency is different, the mean square error is smaller than the conventional method. 4) given the synthetic data from SEM, our propose method works well.

articleTitle: An Improvement of Multi-Party Private Set Intersection Based on Oblivious Programmable PRFs
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Multi-party Private Set Intersection (PSI) allows parties to compute the set intersection of their private data sets without revealing outside the intersection. Kolesnikov et al. (ACM CCS 2017) introduced the Oblivious Programmable Pseudorandom Function (OPPRF) and showed a practical multi-party PSI protocol secure for arbitrary collusion of parties in the semi-honest model. We point out that some OPPRFs in their protocol are overkill to construct it. Based on this observation, we improve their PSI protocol by replacing these OPPRFs with more lightweight procedures. More precisely, we introduce a new functionality called Extended Programmable Pseudorandom Function (EPPRF). It provides functionality that excludes an expensive public-key operation from the OPPRF. We show that a multi-party PSI protocol can be realized even if the OPPRFs are replaced with EPPRFs. As a result of the replacement, we reduce n − 1 public-key operations from Kolesnikov et al.’s protocol, where n is the number of parties.

articleTitle: Sparse Signal Reconstruction with QUBO Formulation in l0-regularized Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: An l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-regularized linear regression for a sparse signal reconstruction is implemented based on the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulation. In this method, the sparse signals are quantized and expressed as bit sequences. By transforming l<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>-norm to a quadratic form of these bits, the quadratic objective function is provided to be optimized by the solver specialized for QUBO, such as the quantum annealer. Numerical experiments with a commercially available quantum annealer show the proposed method demonstrates the reconstruction success rate close to conventional methods based on the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO).

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Computing the Stratonovich’s Value of Information
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We propose an algorithm for computing Stratonovich’s value of information (VoI) that can be regarded as an analog of the distortion-rate function. We construct an alternating optimization algorithm for VoI under a general information leakage constraint and derive a convergence condition. Furthermore, we discuss algorithms for computing VoI under specific information leakage constraints, such as Shannon’s mutual information (MI), f-leakage, Arimoto’s MI, Sibson’s MI, and Csiszár’s MI.A full version of this paper [1] is accessible at: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.02778

articleTitle: On the Optimum Achievable Rates of a Coded Caching Scheme with Small Cache Memory
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In the coded caching scheme proposed by Maddah-Ali and Niesen, we usually consider the setup where K users have the cache memory of size MF and require arbitrary one of N files. Finding the optimum achievable rate of a codeword is one of the fundamental problems of the coded cashing scheme. In this paper, we first consider the case of M = 1/K and give a simplified proof on the achievability part. This result can be extended to the case where the users have cash memory of unequal sizes. We can obtain the optimum achievable rate for this case under a certain assumption. Finally, we consider a new problem on the coded caching where an additional user wants to recover all the files from a codeword and the content of his/her cache memory. We clarify the optimum achievable size of the cash memory of this additional user.

articleTitle: On the Optimal Construction of a Visual Cryptography Scheme for Multiple Secret Images
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: A visual cryptography scheme (VCS) is a secret sharing scheme for digital images. In a VCS, two n × m Boolean matrices, called basis matrices, are used to generate n black-white images called shares from a black-white secret image. Usually, m is called the pixel expansion because the n shares become m times larger than a secret image. So far, minimization of the pixel expansion has been discussed by various authors. In this paper, we consider a VCS that enables the secret sharing of q multiple secret images under q distinct access structures. We give a construction of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sup> basis matrices with the minimum pixel expansion by solving a certain integer programming problem. It is also shown that 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</sup> basis matrices can be explicitly constructed for a certain class of q access structures.

articleTitle: PSOR-Jacobi Algorithm for Accelerated MMSE MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper proposes the Chebyshev periodical successive over-relaxation (PSOR)-Jacobi algorithm for minimum mean squared error (MMSE) detection of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) signals. The proposed algorithm has the advantages of two conventional methods. One is the Jacobi method, which is an iterative method for solving linear equations and is suitable for parallel implementation. It is thus a promising candidate for high-speed simultaneous linear equation solvers for MMSE detector. The other is the Chebyshev PSOR method, which has recently been shown to accelerate the convergence speed of linear fixed-point iterations. We compare the convergence performance of the PSOR-Jacobi algorithm with that of conventional algorithms via computer simulation. The results show that the PSOR-Jacobi algorithm achieves faster convergence without increasing computational complexity, and higher detection performance for a fixed number of iterations. This paper also proposes a fast computation of inverse matrices using the PSOR-Jacobi algorithm.

articleTitle: The Relay Impact on the Physical Layer Security Performance of the Wireless Wiretap Channel
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Information-theoretic analysis of the communication system performances is of practical and theoretical importance. The discrete memoryless wiretap channel with relay and its extension to the continuous alphabet Gaussian version with uncorrelated noises have been studied previously. In this paper, based on Noise-Forwarding (NF) strategy, where the relay node sends codewords independent of the source message to confuse the eavesdropper, the impact of the relay on physical layer security in a Rayleigh fading wiretap channel is studied and closed-form expressions for the probability of positive secrecy rate (PSR), average secrecy rate (ASR), and secrecy outage probability (SOP) are derived. The results, while including previous works as its special cases, show that the relay has positive effects over the PSR, ASR and SOP, as expected intuitively. To support the claims, numerical evaluations are provided.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity with Cost Constraint Allowing Some Cost Overrun
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: A channel coding problem with cost constraint for general channels is considered. Verdú and Han derived ε-capacity for general channels. Following the same lines of its proof, we can also derive ε-capacity with cost constraint. In this paper, we derive a formula for ε-capacity with cost constraint allowing some overrun. In order to prove this theorem, a new variation of Feinstein’s lemma is applied to select codewords satisfying cost constraint and codewords not satisfying cost constraint.

articleTitle: On the Achievability of Interference Channel Coding
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper investigates the achievability of interference channel coding. Codes are constructed by using sparse matrices (with logarithmic column degree) and the constrained-random-number generators, where the rate-splitting technique is unnecessary to achieve known inner regions.

articleTitle: Theory of the optimum interpolation reconstruction and an application for Parallel MRI
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The optimum interpolation reconstruction is applied to parallel MRI reconstruction with multiple receiver coils. We proved mathematically that the proposed method minimizes the upper limit of the approximation error for any other reconstruction method. Numerical simulations of parallel MRI reconstruction from highly under-sampled values of Fourier spectra acquired by four receiver coils were performed on 101 random sampling patterns different from each other. Experimental results showed that the proposed method always generated more accurate MRI images than three reconstruction methods based on three sparse modeling algorithms, CoSAMP, LORAKS, and smoothed FISTA whose hyperparameters are set by using the MATLAB’s Bayesian optimization tool.

articleTitle: PSK-type asymmetric quantum communication and its attenuation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Recent advances in quantum information science based on quantum communications technology will soon be entering the real world. However, the variety of present quantum communication systems is less fruitful than that of modern (classical) communication systems. In the previous paper, we proposed an asymmetric communication system using entanglement and demonstrated a simple example in the noiseless environment. In this paper, we introduce an optimal entangled state in the noiseless environment. Then we show the error performance when using several quantum states in both the noiseless and the attenuated environments.

articleTitle: A Framework for Distributed Source Coding with Encryption: a New Strong Converse and More
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We are interested in investigating the security of encryption schemes for distributed sources coding based on the general framework for distributed sources coding with encryption which Oohama and Santoso proposed in ITW 2021. In particular, we aim to derive the necessary condition, i.e., the strong converse, to guarantee secrecy even when the secret keys are correlated. In this paper, we propose a new metric for the secrecy criterion, defined as the maximum value of mutual information between joint ciphertexts and joint plaintexts from all encryption nodes, where the maximum is taken over all possible distributions of correctly decryptable joint plaintexts. Under our new secrecy criterion, we successfully formulate the rate region, which serves as both necessary and sufficient conditions to have secure transmission even under correlated secret keys. Furthermore, we show that the perfect security under our new secrecy criterion acts as the necessary condition for having the perfect secrecy under the ordinary mutual information in the case that all correctly decryptable joint plaintexts have non-zero probabilities of occurrence.

articleTitle: Lossy Source Coding of Binary Memoryless Source by Trained LDGM Encoder
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Use of low-density generator matrix codes as codebook and encoding with message-passing algorithm is an efficient approach for lossy coding of the i.i.d. binary source. We propose lossy source encoder which is trained on the associated unfolded Tanner graph for improving the rate-distortion performance and/or reducing computational cost.

articleTitle: A Numerical Study of Multi-Letter Ahlswede-Han Scheme for Modulo-Sum Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The achievable sum rate of the multi-letter Ahlswede-Han scheme for the modulo-sum problem is investigated. For auxiliary random variables induced by the parity check matrix of the repetition code, a compact expression of the achievable sum rate in terms of the source distribution’s parameters is obtained. It is numerically demonstrated that the multi-letter Ahlswede-Han scheme strictly improves the sum rate of the Slepian-Wolf scheme and the Körner-Marton scheme for wide ranges of parameters.

articleTitle: New Inner and Outer Bounds for Gaussian Broadcast Channels with Heterogeneous Blocklength Constraints
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We investigate novel inner and outer bounds on the rate region of a 2-user Gaussian broadcast channel with finite, heterogeneous blocklength constraints (HB-GBC). In particular, we introduce a new, modified Sato-type outer bound that can be applied in the finite blocklength regime and does not require the same marginal property. We then develop and analyze composite shell codes, which are suitable for the HB-GBC. Especially, to achieve a lower decoding latency for the user with a shorter blocklength constraint when successive interference cancellation is used, we derive the number of symbols needed to successfully early decode the other user’s message. We numerically compare our derived outer bound to the best known achievable rate regions. Numerical results show that the new early decoding performance in terms of latency reduction is significantly improved compared to the state of the art, and it performs very close to the asymptotic limit.

articleTitle: Influence of Reflected Light in Illumination-Light VN-CodeSK Based Positioning Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper evaluates the effect of reflected light on position error performance when measuring position in the Visible Light Communication (VLC) using the Variable N-parallel Code Shift Keying (VN-CodeSK) system. In particular, the trilateration method and optical fingerprinting method are discussed as positioning systems. Performance results are obtained by computer simulation on a well-known indoor room model. Consequently, it is shown that the trilateration method degrades more sensitively to reflected light than the optical fingerprinting method. The optical fingerprinting method is found to improve accuracy in some cases due to reflected light. In this room model, it is found that the effect of reflected light becomes smaller when the distance from wall is greater than 4[cm].

articleTitle: A Class of Data Compression Where The Codeword Is a Computer Program Generating The Data
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The Kolmogorov complexity of a string is defined as the shortest length of the program on a Turing machine used to represent the string. On the other hand, it is proved that lambda calculus has the same computational power as the Turing machine. This paper proposes a data compression method using computer programs as the codeword. We use the Haskell programming language, which is a functional programming language implemented on the basis of the lambda calculus. As a computational model, we use a context-free grammar and its corresponding computer model, push-down automaton. A relationship between this program and these models is described. In addition to showing the universality of this coding for finite-state information sources, we also show that coding and decoding are possible in linear time.

articleTitle: Finite Blocklength Analysis of Cooperative Superposition Coded Relaying Systems over Nakagami-m Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of cooperative superposition coded relaying systems over quasi-state Nakagami-m channels with finite-blocklength (FLB) transmission. The closed-form expression of the average block error rate (BLER) in decoding a signal with interference over an Nakagami-m channel is derived. By applying this expression to the systems, the closed-form expressions for the BLERs of two nodes are given. Furthermore, the power allocation coefficients and blocklengths are optimized so that the systems' average BLERs are minimum.

articleTitle: Enumeration and Coding of Binary AIFV-m Code Trees
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Sumigawa and Yamamoto gave a method to enumerate all binary AIFV (almost instantaneous fixed-to-variable length) codes using a bijection between binary AIFV code trees and Schröder paths. They also proposed a coding scheme of coding trees based on the enumeration. This paper generalizes Sumigawa and Yamamoto’s method from binary AIFV codes to binary AIFV-m codes. The number of code trees is evaluated based on the bijection between code trees of binary AIFV-m codes and extended Schröder paths with multiple labels. We describe encoding and decoding algorithms for the code trees of AIFV-m codes that count extended Schröder paths sorted in the lexicographic order.

articleTitle: High Areal Density Heated Dot Magnetic Recording Systems with Double-layered Bit Patterned Media
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: An efficient signal processing scheme is proposed for the heated-dot magnetic recording (HDMR) system with double-layered bit-patterned media (BPM). This scheme assumes to be applicable to a HDMR system with total areal density of up to 5.0 Tdpsi. It is cleared that the error rate performance of this HDMR system with double-layered BPM shows significant improvement over the performance of the HDMR system with single-layered BPM by computer simulation.

articleTitle: A Modified MWPM Decoding Algorithm for Quantum Surface Codes Over Depolarizing Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: A quantum surface code is a quantum topological stabilizer code whose stabilizers and qubits are geometrically related. Due to their special structures, surface codes have great potential to be implemented in large-scale quantum computing systems. In the minimum weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoding of surface codes, bit-flip errors and phase-flip errors are assumed to be independent for simplicity. However, these two kinds of errors are likely to be correlated in the real world. In this paper, we propose a modification to the MWPM decoding for surface codes to deal with the noise in depolarizing channels where bit-flip errors and phase-flip errors are correlated. With this modification, we obtain thresholds of 17% and 15.3% for surface codes with mixed boundaries and surface codes with a hole, respectively.

articleTitle: Hash-Chain-Based Sanitizable Signatures for Deletion and Generalization Processes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: As the use of anonymized data with provision to a third party becomes more active, the demand for anonymization agents (AAs), who anonymize data on behalf of the data provider (DP) and pass the anonymized data on to the data recipient (DR), will increase. However, if an AA has malicious intent, the anonymized data may be tampered with.Hash-chain-based sanitizable signature (HSS) is known as a technology to detect cheatings by a malicious AA. In HSS systems, the DP generates a hash chain for the raw data and the candidates of anonymized data by using random values. Then, the DP generates a signature on the hash value at the end of the hash chain and sends it with the raw data to an AA. The AA can only process the raw data to anonymized data in a way that is specified in the hash chain and sends the intermediate hash values of the hash chain with the anonymized data to the DR. If a malicious AA cheats, the DR can detect it by computing the hash value at the end of the hash chain and verifying the signature.However, existing HSS schemes require random values of which number is proportional to that of the raw data and accordingly increase the amount of data communication between the DP, AA, and DR. An HSS scheme requiring a smaller number of random values has also been proposed, but it limits flexibility of AAs’ anonymization.In this paper, we propose an HSS scheme with a small number of random values sent from the DP to an AA without a strict limit to the flexibility of the AAs’ anonymization. Our scheme can encourage the active use of anonymized data.

articleTitle: Generalization Bounds for Deep Transfer Learning Using Majority Predictor Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We analyze new generalization bounds for deep learning models trained by transfer learning from a source to a target task. Our bounds utilize a quantity called the majority predictor accuracy, which can be computed efficiently from data. We show that our theory is useful in practice since it implies that the majority predictor accuracy can be used as a transferability measure, a fact that is also validated by our experiments.

articleTitle: Iterative Model Identification and Tracking with Distributed Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new iterative model identification and tracking technique for distributed sensor systems using a factor graph (FG). The idea is initiated from a position identification technique we proposed [4], however, this paper aims to provide an algorithm which is applicable to more generic identification and tracking purposes. With the proposed technique, each sensor performs signal processing for compression of the measurement data and sends the compressed data to the fusion center. The marginal probability of the compressed sensing results are calculated over the FG at the fusion center. At the final stage, a maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) estimate of the model can be obtained during the tracking phase through the FG. The MAP over FG will be used for the prediction at the next state of model identification to further improve the estimation accuracy without requiring unacceptably high computation effort.

articleTitle: The Maximum Run-Length Constrained Balanced Codes for Random-Access DNA Storage
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: DeoxyriboNucleic Acid (DNA) is a molecule composed of two polynucleotide chains that form a double helix, and each DNA strand contains generic information. DNAs are getting a huge amount of attention these days as new data storage media with ultra high density and long lifespan.When data is stored in DNA strands, some constraints on DNA strands (e.g. the ratio of Cytosine and Guanine within a strand should be 50%, the run-length of each nucleotide is limited up to 5 or the prefix cannot appear within the main data sequence) should be considered for reliability. To examine effectiveness of coding schemes satisfying these constraints, it is important to observe the capacity (the maximum code rate) of such codes. Therefore, in this paper, we present the explicit capacities of codes when certain constraints are given, based on the study of constrained systems. We also observe a coding scheme that focuses on further conditions on the addresses, prefixes of DNA strands appended to identify their positions in the original DNA string, for executing random access in DNA storage.

articleTitle: Bit-Level Informed Dynamic Scheduling for Decoding Non-binary LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Non-Binary Low-Density Parity-Check (NB-LDPC)codes have excellent error rate performance, which outperform their binary counterpart for short and moderate code length. In this work, we propose the first bit-level informed dynamic scheduling decoding algorithm for NB-LDPC codes in binary field. The simulation results show that the proposed decoding algorithm can provide about 1.2 dB gain compared to the state-of-the-art adaptive full bit-reliability-based algorithm (FBRBA). Moreover, the performance can be close to the symbol-based extended min-sum (EMS) decoding algorithm.

articleTitle: A Class of Cyclic Partial Geometries and Their Associated Constant Weight and LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper presents a class of cyclic partial geometries, called triplet partial geometries, which are constructed based on finite fields of characteristic 2. Using these partial geometries, constant-weight codes and LDPC codes with cyclic and quasi-cyclic structure are constructed.

articleTitle: Impact of Artificial Noise Assisted Transmission on the Physical Layer Security Performances in Wireless Wiretap Channel with Active Eavesdropper
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Information-theoretic analysis of the communication systems performances is of practical and theoretical importance. In this paper, we study impact of an artificial noise assisted transmission scheme on physical layer security in a Rayleigh fading wiretap channel with active eavesdropper by deriving closed-form expressions for the average secrecy rate (ASR) and secrecy outage probability (SOP). The results show that artificial noise transmission under active attack has positive effects over secrecy performance of the system model. Numerical evaluations are provided to support the claims.

articleTitle: A Security Enhanced Data Transmission Scheme Using Sequences Generated by Non-Systematic Reed-Solomon Coding
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The authors have proposed a security enhancement scheme using a shortened non-systematic Reed-Solomon codes and discrete Fourier transform over finite fields and the complex field. This study proposes a data transmission method over multi-path channels based on the proposed security scheme.

articleTitle: High-Density Knapsack Cryptosystem using Shifted-Odd and Super-Increasing Sequence
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: It is proven that many public-key cryptosystems would be broken by the quantum computer. The knapsack cryptosystem which is based on the subset sum problem has the potential to be a quantum-resistant cryptosystem. Murakami and Kasahara proposed a new trapdoor sequence of the knapsack cryptosystem which is made by combining shifted-odd sequence and super-increasing sequence. This paper firstly show that the key generation method could not achieve a secure density against the low-density attack. Second, we propose a high-density key generation method and confirmed that the proposed scheme is secure against the low-density attack.

articleTitle: Revisiting Lattice-Based Attacks Using Trace Map for Ring-LWE
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The Ring-LWE problem is one of the mathematical problems underlying the security of lattice-based cryptography, and is defined over the rings of integers of number fields (in particular, cyclotomic fields). In IWSEC 2021, Ikematsu-Nakamura-Yasuda proposed an algorithm for solving the Ring-LWE problem over 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-th cyclotomic fields by using trace maps. They showed that there exist special Ring-LWE samples that enable us to reduce the Ring-LWE problem over 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-th cyclotomic fields to that over their maximal real subfields. However, Ikematsu et al.’s trace map attack is not practical because the probability of obtaining special Ring-LWE samples, which can be used for Ikematsu et al.’s attack, is negligible.In this paper, we revisit Ikematsu et al.’s trace map attack. We show other subfields, which can be attacked, of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-th cyclotomic fields by studying the Galois groups of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-th cyclotomic fields. We give the probability of obtaining a pair of special samples. Our argument about the probability is more precise than Ikematsu et al.’s argument. In addition, we propose and discuss another trace map attack. The difference between our trace map attack and Ikematsu et al.’s attack is conditions of special samples. Our attack is less practical than Ikematsu et al.’s attack but might be improved with sample deformation technique.

articleTitle: A Group-Type Distributed Coded Computation Scheme Based on a Gabidulin Code
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We focus on a distributed coded computation scheme for matrix multiplication. In this system, the product matrix is encoded and decoded through the overall system to correct errors in computation. We propose a group-type distributed coded computation scheme, for one example, a scheme based on a Gabidulin code, and evaluate the computation time complexity and the error-correcting capability of the overall system.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Autoregressive Model with Time-varying Parameters and the Bayes Codes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-dimensional autoregressive model with time-varying parameters as a stochastic image generative model and a lossless image compression algorithm using the Bayes codes. Most studies have relied on Markov chain Monte Carlo methods for Bayesian estimation of autoregressive models with time-varying parameters. However, such a sampling method is not suitable to lossless image compression. Therefore, we propose a Bayes coding algorithm that incorporates image characteristics as hyperparameter settings of an independent conjugate prior distribution. That enables handling the time-varying parameters without any sampling methods. We confirm the properties of the algorithm by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Three-Pass Identification Scheme Based on MinRank Problem with Half Cheating Probability
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In Asiacrypt 2001, Courtois proposed the first three-pass zero-knowledge identification (ID) scheme based on the MinRank problem. However, in a single round of Courtois’ ID scheme, the cheating probability, i.e., the success probability of the cheating prover, is 2/3, larger than half. Although Courtois also proposed a variant scheme which he claimed to have half cheating probability, its security is not formally proven, and it requires another hardness assumption on a specific one-way function and that verifier always generates challenges according to a specific non-uniform distribution.This paper proposes the first three-pass zero-knowledge ID scheme based on the MinRank problem with the cheating probability of exactly half for each round, even with only two-bit challenge space, without any additional assumption. The proposed ID scheme requires fewer rounds and less average total communications costs than Curtois’ under the same security level against impersonation.

articleTitle: Construction of reversible integer codes with large moduli via Chinese remainder theorem
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The codes over rational integer residue rings are called integer codes. In this paper, we give a necessary and sufficient condition concerning the generator matrices when integer codes are to be reversible and show that their reversibility is preserved from the decomposition of integer codes by Chinese remainder theorem. This brings an efficient method for constructing of reversible integer codes with large moduli. Using this method, we enumerate reversible self-dual integer codes of length 3,4 with various moduli. Further, we claim that reversible and self-dual integer codes produce reversible and unimodular lattices, respectively. As a result, we see that the extended binary Hamming code produces the even unimodular lattice of rank 8 and in particular this lattice is reversible, and furthermore the lattice induces an extremal Type II integer code of length 8 with modulus 4.

articleTitle: Ordinary Differential Equation-based Sparse Signal Recovery
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In this paper, continuous-time dynamical systems solving sparse signal recovery problems are presented. The proposed dynamical system is expressed by a nonlinear ODE (ordinary differential equation), which is based on the gradient dynamics involving the gradient of the lasso objective function. The effectiveness of the proposed dynamical system is shown by numerical experiments using the Euler method for solving the proposed ODE. Furthermore, we propose a variational optimization problem for tuning a time-dependent regularization parameter to obtain improved convergence. We propose the deep unfolded-variational optimization (DU-VO) method for solving variational optimization problems. The DU-VO method is applied to the ODE-based sparse signal recovery and the numerical results indicate the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Some Girth-8 Linear Code is a 3-SEQ LRC
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In this paper, we prove that a linear code with girth 8 is a 3-seq LRC with locality r if its parity-check matrix has row weight at most r + 1 and column weight at least 2.

articleTitle: Codes for Constrained Periodicity
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Reliability is an inherent challenge for the emerging nonvolatile technology of racetrack memories, and there exists a fundamental relationship between codes designed for racetrack memories and codes with constrained periodicity. Previous works have sought to construct codes that avoid periodicity in windows, yet have either only provided existence proofs or required high redundancy. This paper provides the first constructions for avoiding periodicity that are both efficient (average-linear time) and with low redundancy (near the lower bound). The proposed algorithms are based on iteratively repairing windows which contain periodicity until all the windows are valid. Intuitively, such algorithms should not converge as there is no monotonic progression; yet, we prove convergence with average-linear time complexity by exploiting subtle properties of the encoder. Overall, we both provide constructions that avoid periodicity in all windows, and we also study the cardinality of such constraints.

articleTitle: A Tighter Lower Bound on the Capacity of the Cascading Binary Deletion Channel and Binary Symmetric Channel
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: The binary deletion channel’s output forms by a subsequence of the transmitted bits. Based on recent research, the capacity bound for the capacity of binary deletion channel is an important subject. In this paper, we will find two tight lower bounds for the first case of 1) only binary deletion channel and 2) cascading binary deletion channel with a binary symmetric channel. Our lower bounds are based on applying the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP) in the first-order Markov model. In our system model, we consider stationary and ergodic binary deletion channel in which bits are deleted with equal probability d. Compared to the well-known lower bounds, our new lower bound improves the capacity lower bound.

articleTitle: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Reconstruction of Circular Binary String based on the Lengths of Substrings with Weights
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: A circular string, which is made by connecting the first and the last symbol of a string, is one of simple sequence forms and is used for many applications such as data compression and fragment assembly problem. A sufficient condition on the lengths of substrings with weights for reconstruction of an input circular binary string is shown. However, there are no detailed descriptions on the proof of the sufficient condition and reconstruction algorithm.In this paper, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition on the lengths of substrings with weights for reconstruction of the circular string. We show the length is shorter than that of previous study for some circular strings. For improving the length, we use minimal absent words (MAWs) for given substrings of length k, and we propose a new construction algorithm of MAWs of length h (> k) while a conventional construction algorithm of MAWs can construct MAWs of length ℓ (≤ k). Moreover, we propose reconstruction algorithm of an input circular string for given substrings satisfying the new condition.

articleTitle: Near-Optimal Designs of Hybrid Massive MIMO Systems from Lattice Decoding
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: A near-optimal design consisting of baseband encoder, finite-resolution analog precoder and combiner for hybrid massive MIMO communications is proposed in this paper. For any configuration of hybrid MIMO systems, several powerful upper bounds on the maximal achievable rates are first presented and are used as design-guidelines. Low-complexity lattice decoders and convex solvers are then employed to find the coefficients of analog precoders and combiners and optimize dynamically the connection structure, aiming to approach the rates of upper bounds. Simulation results show that the proposed design achieves rates within a negligible gap to the upper bounds using phase shifters with only a very small set of PSK signaling and significantly outperforms existing designs.

articleTitle: Average Redundancy of Variable-Length Balancing Schemes à la Knuth
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We study and propose schemes that map messages onto constant-weight codewords using variable-length prefixes. We provide polynomial-time computable formulas that estimate the average number of redundant bits incurred by our schemes. In addition to the exact formulas, we perform an asymptotic analysis and show that our scheme uses $\frac{1}{2}\log n + O(1)$ redundant bits to encode into length-n words with weight (n/2) + q for constant q.

articleTitle: Reconstruction from Substrings with Partial Overlap
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: This paper introduces a new family of reconstruction codes which is motivated by applications in DNA data storage and sequencing. In such applications, DNA strands are sequenced by reading some subset of their substrings. While previous works considered two extreme cases in which all substrings of some fixed length are read or substrings are read with no overlap, this work considers the setup in which consecutive substrings are read with some given minimum overlap. First, an upper bound is provided on the attainable rates of codes that guarantee unique reconstruction. Then, we present efficient constructions of asymptotically optimal codes that meet that upper bound.

articleTitle: Improved Survival Probability for Coded Compressed Sensing in Unsourced Random Access
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In the unsourced random access (U-RA), many users with only a certain number are active in the same time slot. Each user employs the same codebook, and the task of the decoder is to recover a list of transmitted messages regardless of the user’s identity. The compressed sensing(CS) approach is straightforward but with high computational complexity in addressing the U-RA problem. A concatenated coding approach called a coded compressed sensing scheme is a low complexity method that splits each message into L sub-slots. First, an outer tree code connects the messages of all sub-slots. Then, the active users send a column from an inner CS matrix in each sub-slot. However, there is a limitation that the inner CS decoding only decodes the support of a sparse vector, which leads to each user at the same sub-slot must send a different message, and the maximum tolerable active user number is low.We consider the inner CS decoding scheme that first decodes the amplitudes of a sparse vector and quantity them to show the number of active users choosing the same columns. Therefore, the constraint of each user sending different messages at the same sub-slot vanishes, and the maximum tolerable number of active users increases. We first show the maximum tolerable active user number with various codelengths. Next, we improve the survival probabilities’ upper and lower bounds of the outer tree encoder.

articleTitle: Behavioral Authentication Method Focusing on the Tendency of the Days of the Week
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Personal authentication is indispensable in many online services. In the field of this personal authentication research, behavioral authentication using behavioral information stored in smartphones and wearable devices and lifestyle authentication using multiple types of behavioral information have attracted much attention recently. Considering that people have multiple lifestyles and the authentication system, it can be seen that the template will mix the information of multiple lifestyles, and the accuracy of authentication will be reduced. Therefore, it is necessary to prepare multiple templates. Several templates have been used in research on biometrics-based authentication and authentication using behavioral information that has nothing to do with a person’s lifestyle. On the other hand, no such research has been conducted on Wi-Fi information-based authentication. In this paper, we propose a first-step method to solve the problem of mixing multiple lifestyles in a template and reducing authentication accuracy by creating two templates, one for weekdays and the other for holidays, based on Wi-Fi information collected from smartphones. We evaluated the proposed method using actual behavioral data from real-world users in the MITHRA project. We obtained the mean TAR of 0.925 for authentication using weekday data and 0.945 for authentication using holiday data. Looking at the results for individual users, we found that in some cases, accuracy improved, while in others, it did not.

articleTitle: Unified Expression of Utility-Privacy Trade-off in Privacy-Constrained Source Coding
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Privacy-constrained source coding problems have become increasingly important recently, and the utility-privacy trade-off has been investigated for various systems. As pioneering work, Yamamoto (1983) found theoretical limits of the coding rate, privacy and utility in two cases; (i) both public and private information is encoded and (ii) only public information is encoded. However, the theoretical limit has not been characterized in a more general case; (iii) encoded messages consist of public information and a part of private information. Then in this paper, we characterize the trade-off relation in case (iii) using rate-distortion theory. The obtained expression of the achievable region is a "unified expression" because it includes the ones in cases (i) and (ii) as special cases. The numerical results also demonstrate that neither case (i) nor (ii) are the best cases, and it is important to select the encoded information adequately in case (iii).

articleTitle: Sequential Change Detection through Empirical Distribution and Universal Codes
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Universal compression algorithms have been studied in the past for sequential change detection, where they have been used to estimate the post-change distribution in the modified version of the Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) Test. In this paper, we introduce a modified CUSUM test where the pre-change distribution is also unknown and an empirical version of the pre-change distribution is used to implement the algorithm. We present a study of various characteristics of this modified CUSUM Test and then prove its asymptotic optimality.

articleTitle: An analysis of password security risk against dictionary attacks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: In the use of information systems, passwords are a basic means of user authentication and have an important role in practical security. Meanwhile, with the spread of various Internet services in recent years, opportunities for setting passwords are increasing. Therefore, strong passwords are always required to perform the role of user authentication, and the number of research of password is increasing. The main topic of passwords is their quality or strength, i.e., how hard it can be guessed by an attacker, and there are various password strength meters have been proposed so far. In this study, we propose an evaluation method for password strength with the consideration of the risk of dictionary attacks and compare its effectiveness with previous works. By collecting leaked password lists, we build a database and regard it as a Markov information source, whereas previous works regarded it as a memoryless source. Then, we calculate the self-information of the password and use this value to show the risk of dictionary attacks or compare the strength of several passwords. By experiment results, we show that our method is very effective and can help to create effective passwords.

articleTitle: Card-based Cryptographic Protocols for Private Set Intersection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: Card-based cryptography is a cryptographic technique that realizes Multi-Party Computation (MPC) using physical cards. Although various protocols have been studied in card-based cryptography, there is no research on card-based Private Set Intersection (PSI). PSI is one of the well-studied MPC protocols which enables parties to compute the set intersection while keeping their data sets secret. This paper focuses on PSI in card-based cryptography for the first time, and shows several card-based PSI protocols. In card-based cryptography, there are two operation models: one assumes that all operations are performed publicly, and the other allows private operations. We propose PSI protocols under each model. We first show that PSI can be realized under each model by utilizing the existing card-based AND protocols. Furthermore, we propose more efficient PSI protocols than the PSI protocols based on AND protocols under each model.

articleTitle: Balanced coding with Lehmer code
publicationTitle: 2022 International Symposium on Information Theory and Its Applications (ISITA)
abstract: We propose two balanced coding schemes based on the Lehmer code. The first one is very efficient because it is essentially an enumerative coding without any loss. However, it needs an arithmetic device with very long precision proportional to the output block length. The redundancy of the second coding scheme is almost log n, where n is the length of the output block. The scheme needs a list of numbers with length n and lists of numbers with length n/2 in encoding.
